transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-06-14 09:00 PT | Duration 48m | Recorded via Fireflies
Attendees: Jordan Alvarez (Redwood AE), Priya Khatri (Redwood SE), Marcus Chen (Redwood Solutions) --- Lena Ortiz (Head of ML, Vesper Health), David Park (Infra Lead), Maya Singh (Finance), Tom Reynolds (CTO joined at 09:12)

[00:00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. I'm Jordan from Redwood, AE on the account. Quick round robin, who we have on from Vesper?
[00:00:08] Lena: Hi Jordan, Lena here — Head of ML. We're evaluating options to power a patient triage assistant. Low latency, PHI in scope, and budget is quite tight.
[00:00:15] David: David Park, infra. I'll own the pilot infra & network constraints.
[00:00:18] Maya: Maya Singh, finance. I'll be looking at unit economics and pilot spend.
[00:00:22] Priya: Priya Khatri, Redwood SE — I'll handle the performance/benchmark side and work with David on the pilot matrix.
[00:00:30] Jordan: Great. Two things on our side — quick context on Redwood hosting modes and then we want to understand your workload so we can map cost levers: per-token pricing, batching, caching, quantization, and then deployment tradeoffs.
[00:00:44] Lena: Sounds good — our main constraint is 90th percentile latency under 400ms for short chat interactions (ish 50 tokens response). We will also log transcripts for QA but patient data must stay encrypted and access restricted.
[00:00:56] Jordan: Understood. First, can you describe expected volume and request distribution?
[00:01:03] Lena: We expect ~5k daily active users hitting the assistant during daytime, rough QPS peaks ~15-20, mostly single-turn or very short multi-turns. Payloads are small, average prompt ~120 tokens including system message.
[00:01:20] David: Also, some scheduled batch jobs that run nightly for analytics — those can tolerate higher latency.
[00:01:25] Priya: Helpful. So we have two access patterns: interactive low-latency small-responses, and asynchronous batch where cost-efficiency is king.

--- Pricing and unit economics discussion ---
[00:01:40] Jordan: For hosted we bill per-token for generation + per-embedding for vector ops. Typical per-token rates vary by model family; our catalog has small, medium, and large variants and we can recommend quantized variants for cost savings. Do you have target cost per completed interaction?
[00:01:58] Maya: Ideally we'd like < $0.02 per interaction average across mix. If we can get to that with caching/batching, great.
[00:02:06] Jordan: Okay. Quick rule-of-thumb: batching and KV caching can reduce token consumption and effective per-interaction cost by 30–60% depending on hit rates and batch sizes. But batching can add latency — continuous batching with small windows is often a sweet spot.
[00:02:23] Lena: Can you explain KV cache hit assumptions? We have a lot of templated prompts.
[00:02:27] Priya: Sure. KV cache is prefix caching — if users share common system prompts or long contexts we can store KV cache for those prefixes at the server side. For templated prompts, you can see hit rates of 40–70% which reduces tokens sent to model. For example, if a 120-token prompt has a 50% prefix hit, you effectively only generate against 60 tokens plus response tokens. That reduces per-interaction token fee.
[00:02:51] David: Does KV cache work across sessions or only within the same user session?
[00:02:55] Priya: It can be configured. For PHI workloads we often scope caching to tenant or user depending on your privacy rules. With encryption and RBAC we can cache safely at tenant scope.

--- Deployment modes tradeoffs ---
[00:03:10] Jordan: Hosted is fastest to get going and lowest operational overhead. Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools for predictable throughput and slightly better tail latency under high load. Private (VPC/on-prem) addresses data residency and stricter compliance but has higher fixed cost and longer lead time.
[00:03:27] Maya: We're leaning toward hosted for speed, but concerned about PHI compliance and egress controls. How does hosted address SOC2 and customer-managed keys?
[00:03:36] Jordan: Hosted supports SOC2 and we offer KMS integrations for encryption at rest; we also provide audit logs and can set tenant isolation. For full custodian key control we recommend Dedicated or Private, but hosted with customer-managed KMS is often sufficient depending on controls — we'll follow up with SOC2 docs.
[00:03:52] Lena: Good. And on the latency front, if we go hosted and rely on caching/batching, can you guarantee that 90th under 400ms?
[00:03:59] Priya: We can get close for small models and properly tuned batch windows, but guarantees depend on region, model selection, and traffic spikes. With Dedicated and reserved capacity we can set SLO-backed latency buckets. For hosted we provide performance profiles and suggested configs; we should benchmark your exact payload.

--- Quantization and model variants ---
[00:04:20] Jordan: Quantized model variants (8-bit, mixed precision) reduce GPU memory and token cost and are usually slightly slower per-token but much cheaper per-token. For interactive SLOs we can pick the best quantization point.
[00:04:33] Lena: Any accuracy loss we should be worried about in clinical text?
[00:04:36] Priya: There can be small differences — we recommend an eval set. Our Optimize tool can run candidate prompts across model variants and flag regressions.
[00:04:44] Lena: We'll provide a small eval of sensitive prompts.

--- Pilot mechanics ---
[00:04:50] Jordan: Proposed pilot: 2-week hosted pilot using a medium model quantized profile, enable tenant-scoped KV cache, continuous batching with 20–40ms latency window, measure cost per interaction and 90th latency. We'll instrument via the Redwood Console and share token-level cost.
[00:05:06] Maya: Budget? We can commit up to $7k for two weeks if you can show unit cost and path to < $0.02 per interaction.
[00:05:14] Jordan: That seems workable. We'll model expected spend in the pricing spreadsheet and show sensitivity to cache hit rate and quantization.

--- Technical clarifications and interruptions ---
[00:05:24] David: One quick network Q — can the hosted endpoints be restricted to VPC peering? We can't have inbound public traffic.
[00:05:29] Priya: Hosted supports private networking via VPC peering and private endpoints depending on region; there may be an account setup step. For stricter setups we sometimes recommend Dedicated or Private.
[00:05:39] Tom: Sorry for hopping on late — CTO here. My main question: if we scale rapidly what are fallback options? We don't want downtime during spikes.
[00:05:46] Jordan: Fallbacks: routing policies let you fallback to a cheaper compatible model variant or another region; we can also configure burst capacity and automatic fallback to a multi-tenant pool. For mission-critical SLOs Dedicated with reserved capacity is most predictable.

[00:05:59] Lena: Can you walk through an example calculation? Say 1k interactions/day, each response ~40 tokens generated, average prompt 120 tokens but with 50% cache hit on prefix.
[00:06:10] Priya: Rough calc: prompt tokens sent to model ~60 (after 50% prefix hit), plus 40 generated = 100 tokens per interaction. If per-token generation + context rate is $0.00002/token (example mid-tier), that's $0.002 per interaction. With extra overhead (embeddings, logs) maybe $0.003–$0.004. If you get higher cache hit or quantize to cheaper model, you can hit the $0.02 target easily. Note: these numbers are illustrative — we'll tailor in the pricing spreadsheet.
[00:06:39] Maya: Wait — you said $0.002 per interaction? That seems low; does that include context pricing?
[00:06:45] Priya: That was an example using a hypotethical per-token rate; your actual per-token will vary. The point is batching + cache reduces effective tokens and quantization lowers model price. We'll put realistic model rates in the spreadsheet.

--- Objections and tradeoffs ---
[00:06:58] Maya: What's the incremental cost to move to Dedicated? We need to know break-even for steady state if we scale to 1M interactions/month.
[00:07:05] Jordan: Dedicated is a reserved capacity SKU with monthly commit; fixed monthly cost but per-token compute can be lower because of higher utilization and no multi-tenant markup. We can run a break-even analysis given your QPS and utilization — I'll include that in the spreadsheet.
[00:07:18] Lena: For PHI we might need Private, but we need to see the cost delta.
[00:07:22] Jordan: Agreed. Private adds platform licensing/infra costs; it's higher fixed cost but satisfies air-gapped and strict residency. We'll prepare three scenarios: hosted pilot path to reduce unit cost with caching/quant; Dedicated break-even at target volume; Private TCO estimate.

--- Security items raised ---
[00:07:38] David: We'll need SOC2 Type II evidence, encryption controls, and HSM/KMS integration options. Also audit log retention window — can you customize?
[00:07:46] Jordan: Yes — hosted supports audit logs and configurable retention; KMS integrations supported. We'll send SOC2 artifacts and a security FAQ. We'll also schedule a security deep-dive with your SRE/security team next week.

--- Pricing spreadsheet & artifact references ---
[00:07:58] Jordan: We'll share a pricing spreadsheet with model-level rates, sensitivity to cache hit and batch size, and a pilot runbook link.
[00:08:04] Lena: Please include conservative, expected, and optimistic scenarios.
[00:08:07] Jordan: Absolutely.

--- Quick live Q&A about batching windows ---
[00:08:12] Priya: For interactive flows we typically use continuous batching windows of 10–50ms to balance latency vs throughput. You can increase window to 100–200ms if slightly higher latency is acceptable, giving better batching efficiency. For your 400ms SLO we recommend start at 20–50ms windows.
[00:08:29] David: What about GPU memory pressure with quantized models and multiple concurrent sessions?
[00:08:33] Priya: Quantized models reduce memory so you can pack more concurrency per GPU; we also do kernel-level optimizations. Dedicated lets you pin capacity to avoid noisy neighbors.

--- Mid-call recap ---
[00:08:45] Jordan: Recap — pilot on hosted with medium quantized model, tenant-scoped KV caching, 20–40ms batching window, 2 weeks, budget up to $7k. Action items: Jordan send pricing spreadsheet; Priya run hosted micro-benchmark; David share QPS and payload distribution; Maya confirm budget.

--- Late call technical aside (Priya & David) ---
[00:09:12] Priya: Are you using any encryption-in-transit restrictions like mTLS or client certs?
[00:09:15] David: We're standardizing on mTLS when possible.
[00:09:17] Priya: We support mTLS for private endpoints and can layer mutual auth on peering for hosted as well.

--- Closing and next steps ---
[00:09:30] Jordan: Anything else we need to cover?
[00:09:33] Maya: No, but we want the spreadsheet to show the sensitivity curve for cache hits 0–80% and batch windows 10–200ms.
[00:09:41] Jordan: We'll include that.
[00:09:43] Lena: Also include regression testing plan for clinical prompts — we'll upload 200 example prompts.
[00:09:48] Priya: Great — we'll run those across quantized variants and flag any major regressions.
[00:09:53] Jordan: Ok, thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the artifacts and schedule the security deep-dive.
[00:09:58] Tom: Thanks all. Looking forward to the pilot.

Post-call notes: Tom joined 12 minutes into the call. Shared artifacts referenced: pricing spreadsheet (link: drive.redwood/pricing/ve-spreadsheet), pilot runbook (link: drive.redwood/pilots/vesper-pilot), SOC2 pack (link: redwood-sec/soc2). Transcript contains a few transcription errors — proper nouns may be mis-spelled (e.g., "K/V cache" sometimes transcribed as "KVcage"). Recap email to include explicit break-even scenarios and pilot instrumentation plan.
